chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man whom some of the urine of beasts touches: should he wash it or not? He said: “He washes the urine of the donkey, the horse, and the mule. As for the sheep and everything whose meat is eaten, there is no harm in its urine.”

key_terms.أَبْوَالِ: urine; the substance whose ruling is being asked about
key_terms.الْبَغْلِ: the mule, whose urine is to be washed
key_terms.الْحِمَارِ: the donkey, whose urine is to be washed
key_terms.الْفَرَسِ: the horse, whose urine is to be washed
key_terms.بَوْلَ: urine; specifically naming the impurity discussed
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating no problem in this legal context
key_terms.يَغْسِلُهُ: he washes it; indicating the obligation to cleanse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on urine from different animals in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on urine from animals as it pertains to ritual purity. It states that the urine of the donkey, horse, and mule must be washed, while the urine of sheep and other animals whose meat is lawful to eat is not considered problematic in this context.
